title: Researchers Propose Fault-Tolerant Quantum Processor Architecture Controlled by 20 or Fewer External Wires
summary: Researchers have proposed a new fault-tolerant quantum processor architecture that uses 20 or fewer external wires, a significant reduction from current designs. This design features a fixed, clocked planar array where quantum data flows through hard-wired operation tiles. This advancement could lead to more scalable and robust quantum computers. title: Algorithmiq and IBM Quantum Execute 40-Qubit Discrete-Time Quantum Walks on Biological Networks
summary: Algorithmiq and IBM Quantum have successfully executed 40-qubit discrete-time quantum walks (DTQWs) on irregular protein-protein interaction networks, overcoming limitations of conventional dense encodings. They used a sparse single-excitation encoding and novel gate operations to significantly reduce circuit depth. This advancement was applied to a biomedical case study, where quantum walks helped prioritize an asthma risk gene more effectively than classical methods. title: QuTech Demonstrates Weight-Four Stabilizer Parity Checks in a Silicon Spin-Shuttling Processor
summary: Researchers at QuTech have demonstrated significant advancements in quantum computing, showcasing weight-four X- and Z-type quantum error-correction parity checks and five-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) entanglement in a silicon spin-shuttling processor. Their work highlights the successful use of coherent electron shuttling for remote tuning and multi-qubit operations, with an error analysis pointing to two-qubit exchange pulses as the primary source of residual error. title: QuTech Launches Quantum Systems Integration Unit to Build Open-Architecture Superconducting Systems
summary: QuTech has launched a new Quantum Systems Integration Unit to build open-architecture superconducting quantum computers using a European supply chain. The unit aims to standardize modular system interfaces and integrate various hardware and software components, with a planned commercial spinout in 2028. This initiative builds on QuTech's Quantum Inspire platform and incorporates recent research from the DiCarlo Lab to advance quantum error correction. summary: QuTech is coordinating the next 3.5-year phase of the Quantum Internet Alliance (QIA), backed by €47.5 million ($52 million USD) from the European Commission. The program will integrate quantum repeaters, integrated photonics, control electronics, and network software into a programmable full-stack quantum internet prototype. summary: The Dutch HAIQ Consortium, led by Leiden University, secured a €7.4 million NWO grant for a project combining human intuition and AI to optimize quantum control and circuits. title: TU Delft Demonstrates First Hybrid HPC-Quantum Workflow Linking DelftBlue Supercomputer and Tuna-17 Processor
summary: TU Delft and QuTech have successfully linked the DelftBlue supercomputer with QuTech's Tuna-17 quantum processor, demonstrating the first hybrid HPC-quantum workflow. This integration was tested with an electrical power-flow calculation, utilizing the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to optimize circuit parameters and process quantum circuits. title: QuTech and TU Delft Researchers Awarded ERC Synergy Grant to Co-Integrate Spin Qubits and Cryo-CMOS Electronics
summary: QuTech and TU Delft researchers received a six-year ERC Synergy Grant for their UniQ project to scale semiconductor spin-qubit processors. The project aims to overcome wiring and control bottlenecks by co-integrating spin qubits and cryo-CMOS electronics, enabling simplified control and increased qubit connectivity. title: QuTech Demonstrates Coherent Control of a Majorana-Based Qubit in Coupled Kitaev Chains
summary: Researchers at QuTech have successfully demonstrated coherent control of a Majorana-based qubit using coupled Kitaev chains. This qubit, fabricated in an indium antimonide nanowire, operates at 20 mK and exhibits Rabi frequencies of approximately 113-117 MHz. While current coherence times are limited, the team is working on extending the platform to longer chains to improve decoherence and enable advanced operations. title: Generating proteins with complex functions
summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01330-9 A simple generative model learns protein sequence and structure together with functional context, enabling the design of proteins with specified molecular functions and multiple structural states.

title: Exploring nonlinear body oscillations for natural quadruped gaits

The approach offers a design tool to shape embodied intelligence in robotics.

title: A long-context generative foundation model for versatile RNA design
summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01321-w Huang, Lv, Gao and colleagues investigate RNA scaling laws and introduce EVA, a long-context RNA foundation model for function prediction and diverse RNA design, supported by experimental validation.

title: Generating proteins with computationally predicted functions and multiple states via multimodal diffusion
summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01329-2 Jing et al. present ProDiT, a multimodal diffusion model that generates diverse, functionally conditioned proteins, including multistate proteins, expanding capabilities beyond existing generative protein design methods.

title: Accelerating inverse materials design using generative diffusion models with reinforcement learning
summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01334-5 Chen et al. present MatInvent, a reinforcement learning workflow that fine-tunes diffusion models to design crystals meeting single or multiple property targets, with far fewer property calculations than previous methods.

title: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning
summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01332-7 Gowri et al. identify a simple mathematical relationship between the performance of a machine learning model and noise in its training data. The relationship might help to guide machine learning efforts in biology and other fields where data are noisy.

title: New drugs for tuberculosis are put to the test
summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41591-026-00060-0 A phase 2 platform trial tests a plethora of drug combinations that incorporate new agents ganfeborole and BTZ-043 and identifies two regimens for further clinical development.

title: Wastewater sequencing enables scalable measles surveillance
summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04761-4 Integrated clinical and wastewater monitoring during the 2024–2025 outbreaks of measles in South Africa enabled high-resolution tracking of virus spread and evolution. Whole-genome amplicon sequencing of wastewater samples revealed shifts in genotype prevalence, detailed transmission links and previously unreported interprovincial spread.

title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04754-3 Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of wastewater and surveillance samples during the 2024−2025 measles outbreak in South Africa reveal previously undetected inter-provincial spread and transmission links, suggesting that wastewater-integrated whole-genome surveillance can improve measles monitoring and control efforts.

title: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period
summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04530-3 Utah arrays recorded stable spiking activity for up to 7.3 years, with modest signal decline on average and sustained movement decoding in the majority of arrays analyzed, demonstrating the long-term feasibility of intracortical brain–computer interfaces.

summary: 同样是科技巨头宣布加大 AI 投入，资本市场为什么会给出截然不同的反应？ 今年 5 月，我们和老朋友 Aaron 聊过 AI 泡沫与循环投资。半年过去，芯片、数据中心和大模型依然牵动着市场，但投资人追问的问题，逐渐从“还要投入多少钱”，变成了“这些钱，什么时候能赚回来”。 年终总结的第一期，我们再次邀请 Aaron，从英伟达与 Anthropic 聊起，回看科技股起伏背后的预期变化：财报亮眼，为什么股价未必上涨？循环投资的风险，应该从融资结构看，还是从最终需求看？当 AI 从建设基础设施走向应用落地，谁能把技术进步变成持续的收入？回到中国，科技公司过去一年的资源分配与投入节奏，又透露出了怎样的战略选择？ 面对 2027 年，我们没有得到一个确定的涨跌答案，但整理出了几个可以持续观察的信号：真实需求是否增长，投入能否转化为收入，以及产业链上的公司能否支撑自己的现金流。 本期人物 周玖洲 Aaron， 十年中金、华夏基金等顶级投资机构工作经验，「涉市未深」、「不止金钱」主播， Yaxian，《What’s Next｜科技早知道》主播 本期话题 [03:18] 半年之后重新看，AI 泡沫到了哪一步？ 股价涨幅、企业估值和融资结构是不同的衡量尺度，选择哪把尺子，会影响我们对 AI 泡沫大小的判断。 预期降温并不必然意味着技术失去前景，产业仍可能在市场热情回落后，进入应用逐步普及的阶段。…
